calls.head: Special teams lean toward the Golden Knights
calls.body: The Sharks’ penalty kill is one of the league’s worst, and the Golden Knights’ power play is one of the best. Discipline matters more than usual for the Sharks tonight.

calls.head: The Golden Knights are likely to tilt the ice
calls.body: The Golden Knights have been near the top of the league at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Sharks one of the worst. Expect the Golden Knights to spend more of the night in the Sharks’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

surprises.head: San Jose flipped the shot count
surprises.body: San Jose allows more shots than almost anyone. Not tonight: San Jose took 53 of the 81 shot attempts at 5-on-5. From how these two usually play, San Jose would expect about 45%. A team strays this far about once every 300 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

surprises.head: Vegas couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: San Jose usually allows more dangerous shots than most teams. Not tonight: Vegas’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 4.3% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.5% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 45 games.

story.head: Gaudette has a goal and an assist as the Sharks take down the Golden Knights
paras: Michael Misa got the scoring started for the Sharks late in the second. It was a busy third period. Adam Gaudette stretched the lead to 2-0 early in the period, with Dmitry Orlov picking up his 300th NHL assist on the goal. Jack Eichel cut San Jose’s lead to 2-1 on the power play midway through the period, but that was as close as they got. Zack Ostapchuk extended the lead to 3-1 with just under six minutes left. Macklin Celebrini added an empty-net goal with a little over two minutes left to make it 4-1.

The Sharks carried the play, outshooting the Golden Knights 33-28 (25-14 at 5-on-5), and got the result to match. Yaroslav Askarov made 27 saves for the Sharks, and Carter Hart kept the Golden Knights in it, stopping 29 of 32. By our Swing measure, Alexander Wennberg had the best night of anyone. The Sharks improved to 12-14-2 and climbed to third in the Pacific, while the Knights fell to 15-7-5, second in the Pacific.
